reason: The cited evidence (E1) demonstrates synthesis of HEA nanoparticles on granular supports and their catalytic stability, but it provides no data or discussion on premelting, melting behavior, or the effect of support anchoring on thermal stability. The key mechanistic premises about interfacial bonding suppressing surface diffusion and delaying premelting are therefore unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Strong metal–support interactions (e.g., on defect-rich carbon) limit surface atomic mobility
Suppressed surface diffusion delays premelting onset and increases melting temperature
Unsupported nanoparticles lack interfacial stabilization and premelt at lower temperatures
The effect is significant and reproducible for ~2–10 nm HEA nanoparticles
